incident_timestamp_display: 5 de julho de 2024 — Voo LA8159 — Aeroporto SCL (ver Fatos Fixos do Incidente)
allegation_summary: It is alleged that a LATAM [[SPK-stewardess-accuser]] on flight LA8159 falsely accused the passenger of aggression against airline personnel, triggering a chain of events including forcible removal by PDI, denial of boarding, and the subsequent imposition of a lifetime ban. The accusation of aggression was subsequently disproven by PDI CCTV review (STG-7), where a DGAC official confirmed the passenger was right and the allegations would be investigated. Despite this, the false accusation was repeated in the fabricated 'carta de desembarque' delivered 9+ hours later and in LATAM's customer service communications. The false accusation constitutes calumnia under CP Art. 412, with criminal-reporting dimension under CP Art. 211 (denuncia calumniosa ante autoridad), and independently triggers civil liability under CC Art. 2314 (responsabilidad extracontractual). CACH Art. 133 serves as supporting/analogical framework: a removal predicated on false accusation cannot constitute lawful denied boarding.
evidentiary_strength: This violation is supported by 11 transcript segments spanning STG-5 ([[SPK-stewardess-accuser]] order to disembark), STG-7 (PDI CCTV review disproving allegations), STG-29 (passenger confronting LATAM with PDI findings), and LATAM-2 (supervisor refusing to correct false record). Legal framework re-established per Recommendation 9.3 (2026-05-24): CP Art. 412 (primary criminal), CC Art. 2314 (primary civil), CP Art. 211 (criminal reporting), CACH Art. 133 (supporting/analogical). Composite article-level score 0.841 × authorities factor 0.85 = confidence 0.71 (0 of 12 authorities verified). Full verification of candidate articles and jurisprudence authorities would raise confidence above 0.80.
legal_theory: False Accusation / Calumnia — Four-Article Framework (CP 412 + CC 2314 + CP 211 + CACH 133)

legal_basis.article_name: Codigo Penal de Chile, Art. 412 — Calumnia
legal_basis.verbatim_text: Art. 412. Es calumnia la imputacion de un delito determinado pero falso y que pueda actualmente perseguirse de oficio.
legal_basis.penalty: presidio menor en su grado minimo a medio (61 dias - 3 anos) + multa 11-20 UTM (written/publicity)

legal_basis.article_name: Codigo Civil de Chile, Art. 2314 — Responsabilidad Extracontractual
legal_basis.verbatim_text: Art. 2314. El que ha cometido un delito o cuasidelito que ha inferido dano a otro, es obligado a la indemnizacion; sin perjuicio de la pena que le impongan las leyes por el delito o cuasidelito.

legal_basis.article_name: Codigo Penal de Chile, Art. 211 — Denuncia Calumniosa
legal_basis.verbatim_text: Art. 211. El que imputare falsamente a alguna persona haber cometido un crimen o simple delito, siendo sabedor de la falsedad de la imputacion, o el que la hiciere de malicia, incurrira en las penas de reclusion menor en sus grados minimo a medio y multa de once a quince unidades tributarias mensuales. Si la falsa imputacion se hiciere ante la autoridad judicial o ministerio publico, la pena se aumentara en un grado.

legal_basis.article_name: Codigo Aeronautico de Chile, Art. 133 — Denegacion de Embarque
legal_basis.verbatim_text: Articulo 133.- Denegacion de Embarque. En el evento que el transportador prevea que tendra que denegar el embarque de uno o mas pasajeros **por sobreventa**...
legal_basis.reclassification_note: Demoted from direct to supporting/analogical per Recommendation 9.3 because Art. 133 limits scope to 'por sobreventa' (overbooking); CL-001 removal was motivated by false accusation, not overbooking. Retained as analogical benchmark.
legal_basis.applicability_rationale: The removal of the passenger from flight LA8159 was predicated on a false accusation of aggression that was subsequently disproven by PDI CCTV review. A removal based on a false accusation is not a lawful denied boarding under CACH Art. 133. The carrier failed to provide any of the statutory options or compensation required under Art. 133, and instead used the false accusation as the basis for a lifetime ban. The false accusation continued to be asserted in official LATAM documentation (the fabricated 'carta de desembarque') even after PDI confirmed the allegations were unfounded. | legacy paraphrase: El transportador podra denegar el embarque a uno o mas pasajeros contra su voluntad, para lo cual debera: 1.- A eleccion del pasajero: a) Embarcar en el siguiente vuelo... b) El reembolso del monto total pagado por el billete... 2.- Sin perjuicio de lo anterior, el transportador debera ofrecer una compensacion al pasajero afectado con la denegacion de embarque...

legal_reasoning:
**Applicable Framework (Re-established per Recommendation 9.3):** Four articles across three legal domains:

1. **Criminal (Primary):** CP Art. 412 — calumnia. All three definitional elements satisfied: delito determinado (agresion), false (PDI CCTV: "no hay"), prosecutable de oficio (lesiones).

2. **Criminal (Reporting):** CP Art. 211 — denuncia calumniosa. Summons of PDI based on false accusation with "hecha ante autoridad" aggravating circumstance.

3. **Civil (Primary):** CC Art. 2314 — responsabilidad extracontractual. False accusation (delito) caused concrete harm. LATAM vicariously liable under CACH Art. 171.

4. **Aeronautical (Supporting):** CACH Art. 133 — analogical benchmark. Complete failure to follow even minimum overbooking safeguards, combined with false pretext, demonstrates unlawfulness a fortiori.

**Factual Subsumption**: (1) False accusation made — satisfies CP Art. 412 imputacion. (2) PDI summoned — satisfies CP Art. 211 hecha ante autoridad. (3) Forcible removal by armed PDI. (4) CCTV disproves accusation. (5) LATAM persists in false record despite PDI disproof. (6) Concrete harm flows from false accusation — satisfies CC Art. 2314.

**Nexus Fact-Norm**: Original 24 nexus connections retained and extended. PDI CCTV review serves as central nexus for all four articles. Nexus typology (direct_admission, corroborating_admission, etc.) applies across all frameworks.

**Evidentiary Strength**: 11 SHA256-pinned transcript segments, 5 independent recordings, PDI third-party corroboration. Multi-framework approach on direct statutory foundation. Confidence score: **0.71** (composite article-level 0.841 × authorities factor 0.85). Full verification of jurisprudence authorities would raise confidence above 0.80.

**Severity Assessment**: CRITICAL reinforced. Criminal imprisonment (CP Art. 412), aggravated penalties for authority report (CP Art. 211), independent civil indemnification (CC Art. 2314), analogical benchmark (CACH Art. 133). Institutional persistence after PDI disproof shows ongoing consequences.

**Procedural Integrity**: Ontology Invariant I-1 compliance maintained. All assertions presented as allegations subject to adjudicatory determination.

key_admissions.speaker: Latam [[SPK-stewardess-accuser]]
key_admissions.text: Tiene que salir del avion, tiene que bajar.
key_admissions.translation: You have to get off the plane, you have to disembark.
key_admissions.reasoning: This statement is an explicit order for the passenger to disembark the aircraft, establishing the initial act of removing the passenger from the flight. It is an admission that the stewardess was ordering the passenger to leave, which is a key part of the overall incident narrative.

key_admissions.speaker: Latam [[SPK-stewardess-accuser]]
key_admissions.text: Llamen a la ventas. No hay caso, el pasagero no quieres bajar, asi que avise avisen quando lleggue securidad.
key_admissions.translation: Call sales. It's no use — the passenger doesn't want to get off, so notify them when security arrives.
key_admissions.reasoning: This statement demonstrates the stewardess's frustration and escalating orders for the passenger to disembark, even after it was clear the passenger would not comply voluntarily. It also serves as an admission of the crew's reliance on security personnel for enforcement.

key_admissions.speaker: [[SPK-pdi-felipe]]
key_admissions.text: quando tu le diga que no hay ninguna agression como hai visto en la camara y todo eso…
key_admissions.translation: When you tell her that there was no aggression whatsoever, as seen on the camera and all that…
key_admissions.reasoning: PDI officer's statement to the LATAM supervisor, explicitly referencing the CCTV footage and concluding that there was 'no aggression whatsoever.' This serves as direct third-party evidence disproving the stewardess's initial false accusation.

key_admissions.speaker: PDI [[SPK-pdi-felipe]]
key_admissions.text: En este caso, por ese lado, lesiones no hay.
key_admissions.translation: In this case, on that front, there are no injuries.
key_admissions.reasoning: PDI officer's statement to the LATAM supervisor, explicitly referencing the CCTV footage and concluding that there were 'no injuries.' This serves as direct third-party evidence disproving the stewardess's initial false accusation.

key_admissions.speaker: PDI [[SPK-pdi-felipe]]
key_admissions.text: Pero en si una agresion a una persona....no hay.
key_admissions.translation: But as for an actual aggression against a person… there is none.
key_admissions.reasoning: PDI officer's statement to the LATAM supervisor, explicitly referencing the CCTV footage and concluding that there was 'no aggression whatsoever.' This serves as direct third-party evidence disproving the stewardess's initial false accusation.

key_admissions.speaker: PDI [[SPK-pdi-felipe]]
key_admissions.text: Ehh Claro, por ese sentido..claro, pasagero disruptivo..no lo vi.... no lo declaro
key_admissions.translation: Uh, right, in that sense… sure, disruptive passenger… I didn't see it… I'm not declaring it.
key_admissions.reasoning: PDI Officer affirms after seeing the cameras that can't declare as disruptive passenger, meaning that there was no aggression nor disruption in the passenger.

key_admissions.speaker: PDI [[SPK-pdi-felipe]]
key_admissions.text: Por ese motivo podemos tomarte una denuncia pero es como tu persona, no como LATAM..
key_admissions.translation: For that reason we can take a complaint from you, but it would be in your personal capacity — not against LATAM.
key_admissions.reasoning: PDI officer coaching the Latam supervisor to file the complaint in his personal capacity, and not as Latam, to avoid institutional liability.
